rows.subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
rows.description: A teenager notices that fluent English earns respect at school while a regional language is treated as lesser. Language is not intelligence; noticing this bias helps the teen resist it in themselves and others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
rows.description: A young adult feels strong love for their state's language and bristles at Hindi or English being imposed. Pride is healthy; contempt for another language is not, and friendships cross these lines easily.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, contempt, pride

rows.subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
rows.description: A student in a new state struggles at shops and in class and feels an outsider. Learning basic phrases and being patient with mistakes wins goodwill; locals can help by slowing down.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
rows.description: A young adult moves between casual home speech and polished professional English without feeling fake. Each register is a tool, and keeping the mother tongue alive keeps the person whole.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Village child in a city school [Receiver]
rows.description: A child moving from a village to a town school notices different clothes, words and manners and feels behind. Encouragement, patient teaching and a friend to sit with can turn shame into confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A city child on a holiday sees animals, fields and a slower rhythm and is thrilled by mud and mangoes. It is easy to romanticise; the child may learn later of hard work behind such simplicity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a village studies by lamp and dreams of an engineering or civil service career in a city. Determination is strong, but money, coaching gaps and family need can slow it; local mentors matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A city teenager faces crowded schools, tuition, traffic and comparison on social media, with little open space. Speed and choice are real gains, but stress and loneliness follow if nothing balances them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Looked down on as gaon wala [Receiver]
rows.description: A young adult from a village is mocked in a city college for accent or dress. Pride in roots and steady friends help; peers who include the person show more class than those who tease.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A villager sees urban youth as selfish, disconnected from family and soil. This is partly true of some and unfair to many; both sides carry stereotypes worth unlearning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
